sections.title: Climate
sections.filled: Across the surrounding basin of about 11,888 km², rainfall averages about 246 mm a year, moderately seasonal, with August the wettest month. Temperatures there average 9.9 °C, from -2.3 °C in January to 22.4 °C in July. Its aridity index of 0.19 falls in the UNEP arid class. Of the eight basins that meet here, it receives the least precipitation and is the most arid. Its basin is warmer than four of the seven basins around it.

sections.title: Land and geology
sections.filled: Across the basin, the land is gently sloping on average (a mean slope of 4.5%), with topsoil that averages 52% sand, 32% silt and 16% clay (USDA texture class: loam). The underlying rock is mostly siliciclastic sedimentary rocks. Karst outcrop covers up to about 3% of the basin.

sections.title: Land cover around 2000
sections.filled: Around 2000, about 1% of the basin is cropland and 66% is pasture; in the GLC2000 land cover map, the commonest class other than cultivated land is shrub cover, closed-open, deciduous (with or without sparse tree layer), at about 59%. Compared with the seven basins around it, its basin has more pasture than all but one and less forest than all but one.

sections.title: Surroundings
sections.filled: Chaco Canyon's basin is one of eight that meet here. None of them drains into it. It drains into one of them. The basins across its divides all receive more precipitation. Of the eight basins that meet here, it has the gentlest slopes.
